title: VP, SOX Compliance and Internal Controls Leader
description: At Broadridge, we've built a culture where the highest goal is to empower others to accomplish more. If you’re passionate about developing your career, while helping others along the way, come join the Broadridge team. The VP, SOX Compliance and Internal Controls Leader will lead the Company’s SOX program and overall internal control framework. This role will own the end-to-end design, governance, scope, methodology and related documentation the SOX program. The role will directly lead a team of three SOX professionals and serve as the primary liaison to Internal and External audit. This leader will coordinate testing activities with the Internal Audit SOX testing team, review reported observations and exceptions, monitor progress, and formulate management’s conclusions regarding design and operating effectiveness. This individual will look for ways to continuously improve the program, including automation of controls and enhanced use of reporting tools. The successful candidate will bring strong technical judgment, a disciplined operating approach, and the ability to communicate complex control matters clearly to senior leadership and control owners. Key Responsibilities SOX Program Leadership and Governance Lead and continuously enhance the Company’s SOX PMO, including management, development, and prioritization of a three-person team. Own the annual and ongoing SOX program plan, governance model, calendar, deliverables, escalation protocols, and status reporting. Present management’s SOX status, conclusions, deficiencies, remediation progress, scope changes, and emerging risks to senior management and relevant governance stakeholders. Oversee the development and maintenance of documentation supporting management’s SOX assessment and conclusions. Lead program enhancements, automation/AI, or maturity initiatives for SOX processes; look for ways to leverage testing in other areas (e.g. SOC) to streamline company-wide testing requirements. Deliver training and guidance to control owners on SOX requirements, controls documentation, evidence expectations, deficiency management, and evolving program requirements. Methodology, Documentation, and Assessments Establish, maintain, and enhance the Company’s SOX methodology, including standards for Risk and Control Matrices (RCMs), sampling policy, deficiency evaluation framework, quarterly management attestations. Maintain full responsibility for SOX scoping, including significant accounts and disclosures, in-scope applications, interfaces, in-scope controls, key spreadsheets, entity-level controls (ELCs), outsourced service providers Oversee the maintenance high-quality process narratives, RCMs, control descriptions, evidence standards, and other SOX documentation. Monitor walkthroughs and align timing with Internal Audit and Deloitte. Co-lead walkthroughs with Internal Audit and facilitate timely resolution of questions, evidence requests, and documentation matters. Internal and External Audit Coordination Serve as the primary point of contact for the SOX PMO’s relationship with Internal Audit and external audit. Coordinate with Deloitte and Internal Audit to support a well-managed, efficient, and timely audit process. Agree with Internal Audit on the annual test plan, testing approach, timing, and reporting cadence. Monitor SOX testing progress and status as reported by Internal Audit; identify risks to timelines and drive appropriate escalation. Review and agree to proposed changes to test scripts from Internal Audit. Oversee the review Internal Audit reports for observations, exceptions, and other control findings. Review Internal Audit testing results and evaluate their implications for management’s SOX assessment. Conclude on design and operating effectiveness based on management’s assessment and Internal Audit testing results. Deficiency Evaluation and Remediation Lead the assessment of control deficiencies, including aggregation, severity assessment, management conclusions, and escalation. Partner with process and control owners to develop practical remediation plans, establish accountable owners and due dates, and monitor execution. Escalate significant remediation risks, overdue actions, and matters that may affect management’s SOX conclusions. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, Information Systems, or a related field. CPA, CIA, CISA, or similar professional certification strongly preferred. 12+ years progressive experience leading SOX compliance, internal controls, internal audit, external audit, or financial-risk programs within a public company environment. Experience in a publicly traded fintech, technology, or similar environment strongly preferred Experience with Optro (Audit Board) technology strongly preferred. Demonstrated experience leading a SOX PMO or comparable internal-controls function, including ownership of scope, methodology, testing coordination, deficiencies, remediation, and conclusions. title: Senior Director, Enterprise Compliance
description: Hi, we're Oscar. We're hiring a Senior Director, Enterprise Compliance to join our Compliance team. Oscar is the first health insurance company built around a full stack technology platform and a relentless focus on serving our members. We started Oscar in 2012 to create the kind of health insurance company we would want for ourselves—one that behaves like a doctor in the family. About the role: The Senior Director, Enterprise Compliance supports the execution and continuous improvement of Oscar's enterprise compliance program. Reporting to the Chief Compliance Officer, you will provide leadership over key compliance functions, including regulatory compliance, regulatory change management/implementation, compliance operations, investigations, monitoring and auditing, policy governance, and compliance education. You will anticipate regulatory and industry developments, translates them into enterprise compliance priorities, and partners with cross-functional leaders to identify and mitigate compliance risks, strengthen internal controls, and promote a culture of ethics and integrity. You will exercise significant independent judgment, develops a compliance organization, and serves as a trusted advisor to business leaders on complex healthcare regulatory matters. You will report into the Vice President, Chief Compliance Officer. Work Location: This position is based in our Tempe, AZ office, requiring a hybrid work schedule with 3 days of in-office work per week. Thursdays are a required in-office day for team meetings and events, while your other two office days are flexible to suit your schedule. #LI-Hybrid Pay Transparency: The base pay for this role is: $196,733 - $258,212 per year.. You are also eligible for employee benefits, participation in Oscar's unlimited vacation program, company equity grants and annual performance bonuses. Responsibilities: Lead the execution and continuous improvement of Oscar's enterprise compliance program, including the multi-year compliance strategy, annual compliance work plans, risk assessments, policy governance, regulatory change management/implementation, monitoring, auditing, and reporting activities. Translate enterprise compliance priorities into an relevant operating plan; establish ownership and governance; allocate resources; develop compliance managers and team members; remove barriers; and lead accountability for measurable outcomes. Anticipate regulatory and industry developments and advise senior leaders on their possible effects for Oscar's products, market participation, business strategy, and operating model. Provide guidance on federal and state healthcare regulations, contractual obligations, and emerging regulatory risks across applicable lines of business. Oversee compliance investigations, hotline reporting, the Special Investigations Unit, fraud-prevention activities, corrective action plans, and remediation efforts, ensuring timely resolution and appropriate escalation of significant compliance concerns. Partner with leaders across Legal, Privacy, Security, Internal Audit, Enterprise Risk, Clinical, Product, Operations, and People teams to embed compliance requirements into business processes and strategic initiatives. Set and uphold enterprise standards for ethics and compliance by leading education, communications, and awareness initiatives that strengthen Oscar's culture of ethics and compliance. Lead compliance reporting and engagement for executive leadership, Compliance Committee, Board committees, and regulatory examinations; support interactions with regulators and external auditors. Compliance with all applicable laws and regulations Other duties as assigned Requirements: 12+ years of progressively responsible experience in healthcare compliance, regulatory affairs, legal compliance, audit, or enterprise risk management. 5+ years leading high-performing compliance teams and enterprise-wide compliance initiatives. Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, and maintaining an effective healthcare compliance program aligned with OIG Compliance Program Guidance and applicable federal and state regulations. Experience supporting highly regulated healthcare organizations, including health plans, managed care organizations, healthcare technology companies, provider organizations, or related entities. Track record of anticipating regulatory developments and translating them into enterprise priorities, operating plans, and business controls. Demonstrated experience leading complex compliance investigations, monitoring and auditing activities, regulatory risk assessments, corrective action planning, and policy governance. Experience advising senior business leaders on complex regulatory and operational compliance issues and leading their resolution Strong written and verbal communication skills, experience presenting to executive leadership, governance committees, regulators, or external auditors. The ideal candidate is self-sufficient, strategic, and able to quickly get up to speed in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. WHAT YOU WILL DO Support the BSA Officer in the development, implementation, and ongoing enhancement of a comprehensive BSA/AML and Sanctions compliance program aligned with U.S. regulatory expectations and global best practices. Oversee and manage key components of the BSA/AML and Sanctions program, including transaction monitoring, investigations, data validation, reporting, and recordkeeping functions, ensuring operational effectiveness and regulatory compliance. Respond to and support banking partner due diligence (DD) requests, ensuring timely, accurate, and comprehensive information is provided to maintain strong partner relationships. Lead and execute strategic initiatives and special projects related to financial crimes compliance, systems, and operational scalability. Strong working knowledge of U.S. BSA/AML regulations, OFAC requirements, and financial crimes compliance frameworks. Demonstrated ability to operate independently, take ownership of complex initiatives, and drive programs forward with minimal oversight. Experience overseeing investigations, SAR filings, and regulatory reporting obligations. Strong understanding of risk assessments, control design, and program governance. Proven experience managing regulatory exams, audits, and remediation efforts. Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess risk and make sound, defensible decisions. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present to senior management and regulators. Ability to work cross-functionally and influence stakeholders across business, product, and engineering teams. Highly organized with strong project management capabilities and attention to detail. Champion the three-part controls model - prevent it, decide it, prove it stays right - and drive enterprise-wide adoption across platform services and leadership stakeholders. Act as the primary bridge to C-suite, legal, and risk stakeholders - keeping governance conversations productive and release schedules on track. Bachelor's/ Masters degree in engineering, computer science, or a related field; advanced degree or relevant certifications strongly.
